{{short description|American physicist}}
'''Stanley J. Brodsky''' (born January 9, 1940) is an American [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] and emeritus professor in the [[SLAC Theory Group]] at the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]] at [[Stanford University]].

==Biography==

Brodsky obtained an undergraduate degree in 1961 and Ph.D. in physics in 1964 from the [[University of Minnesota]], where his advisor was [[Donald R. Yennie]].  After two years as a research associate for [[Tsung-Dao Lee]] at [[Columbia University]], in 1966 he began working for SLAC, where he became a professor in 1976.<ref name="winner"/>

Brodsky's research has focused on [[quantum chromodynamics]], which is the theory describing the [[strong interaction]]s between [[quark]]s and [[gluon]]s.  His 1973 paper co-authored with [[Glennys Farrar]], ''Scaling Laws at Large Transverse Momentum'' (''[[Physical Review Letters|Phys. Rev. Lett.]]'' 31, 1153–1156), and 1980 paper with Peter Lepage, ''Exclusive Processes in Perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics'' (''[[Physical Review|Phys. Rev. D]]'' 22, 2157–2198), led to the award of the Sakurai Prize.<ref name="discover">Hewett, JoAnne (October 9, 2006). [https://www.discovermagazine.com/the-sciences/prizes-galore Prizes Galore!], ''[[Discover (magazine)]]''. Accessed April 10, 2025.</ref>

He was the 2007 recipient of the [[Sakurai Prize]] for Theoretical Particle Physics, "for applications of [[Perturbation theory (quantum mechanics)|perturbative quantum field theory]] to critical questions of elementary particle physics, in particular, to the analysis of hard exclusive strong interaction processes."<ref name="winner">[http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Brodsky&first_nm=Stanley&year=2007 2007 J.J. Sakurai Prize for Theoretical Particle Physics Recipient], aps.org, Retrieved October 8, 2012</ref><ref name="slac">Plummer, Bard. (October 9, 2006). [http://today.slac.stanford.edu/feature/sakurai-prize-06.asp SLAC Theoretical Physicist Stanley J. Brodsky Awarded Sakurai Prize], [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|SLAC]] Today. Accessed February 19, 2024.</ref> He received the [[Pomeranchuk Prize]], an international award for theoretical physics in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SLAC’s Stanley Brodsky Shares Pomeranchuk Prize for Theoretical Physics |url=https://www6.slac.stanford.edu/news/2016-01-08-slacs-stanley-brodsky-shares-pomeranchuk-prize-theoretical-physics |access-date=2025-04-24 |website=SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory |language=en}}</ref>
